_comment: Hand-authored. Bank 6 object handlers: tile animator $7B and the eyes $7E/$7F ($B7BD-$B901). The generators subtract these.

regions.name: TYPE $7B (AN INVISIBLE TILE ANIMATOR): first frame?
regions.description: TYPE $7B (AN INVISIBLE TILE ANIMATOR): Type bit 7 set goes to the animation (`$B7C8`). Table stats: collision flags `$CA`, hit points 1, attack 1, drawing flags 0, never drawn as a sprite. **It animates a background tile by rewriting CHR RAM.**

regions.description: X := 0 for poses 0 and 1, 5 for poses 2 and 3; poses 1 and 2 add 12: the two shapes at `$B839` / `$B845`, read forwards (poses 0, 1) or backwards (poses 2, 3, i.e. upside down).

regions.description: `LDX $15`; `JMP $C03F` (`$D6F7`: the queue item is complete). RUN: the item `0E 1F D1` + 14 bytes was queued at the start of every pose (frames 7, 15, 23, 31 ...), e.g. pose 1: `30 6C 4C 52 66 3C 00 00 3C 72 52 5E 66 3C`. The blank-looking `FD` tiles in the stage pictures (the rubble blocks) are therefore NOT blank: this object makes them change. NOT established: what the picture looks like on screen, or which stage uses `$7B`.

regions.name: Type $7B tile rows: 2 shapes x [6 low-plane bytes][6 high-plane bytes]
regions.description: `0C 36 32 4A 66 3C | 3C 4E 4A 7A 66 3C` and `30 6C 4C 52 66 3C | 3C 72 52 5E 66 3C`: the low-plane and the high-plane rows (1-6) of the animated tile; poses 2 and 3 read them backwards. The high-plane bytes are at `$B83F + X`.

regions.description: TYPES $7E / $7F (THE EYES OF THE STAGE BOSSES): Type bit 7 set goes to `$B890`. Table stats: collision flags `$7A`, hit points 24, attack 32, drawing flags 0, **dies as the block blast (type `$30`)**. Ground objects made from the stage's metatiles; **no area scaling**. After the initialisation the type is `$FE` / `$FF`, which is how the table reads below are indexed.
